tx.t: In this talk I would like to tell the story of chocolate. Chocolate comes from the seeds of the cacao tree, which first grew in Central and South America.

The Maya and the Aztecs drank a bitter chocolate drink, often with chilli, and sometimes used the beans as money. Spanish explorers brought cacao to Europe in the sixteenth century, and people began to add sugar.
The first solid eating chocolate was made by an English company, Fry, in eighteen forty-seven. Milk chocolate was invented by a Swiss man, Daniel Peter, in eighteen seventy-five.

The scheme soon met a serious problem: too few bikes in the hills. The council solved it with a van that moves bikes uphill every morning.
Today, a ride costs two pounds fifteen for the first half hour, and the first fifteen minutes are free for residents.

items.title: Ulugh Beg and the Samarkand Observatory

tx.t: Today I would like to tell you about Ulugh Beg, the ruler and astronomer of Samarkand. Ulugh Beg was a grandson of the conqueror Timur, and he ruled Samarkand in the first half of the fifteenth century.
He built a great observatory in Samarkand in the fourteen twenties. Its main instrument was a giant sextant, with a radius of about forty metres.
With it, his team made a catalogue of more than a thousand stars that was used for centuries. His measurement of the length of the year was wrong by less than a minute.

tx.t: Today I will explain how the human heart works. The heart has four chambers: two at the top, called atria, and two at the bottom, called ventricles.
At rest, the adult heart beats between sixty and one hundred times every minute. Over a day, that adds up to roughly one hundred thousand beats.
The heart pumps about five litres of blood around the body every minute. The heart of an adult weighs only about three hundred grams, and it is about the size of a clenched fist.
Regular exercise makes the heart stronger, so it can pump more blood with each beat.

tx.t: Let me tell you something about the history and the economics of coffee. According to legend, coffee was discovered in Ethiopia by a goat herder called Kaldi, who noticed that his goats became lively after eating the berries.

By the fifteenth century, coffee was grown in Yemen, and it then spread to Turkey and Europe. There are two main kinds of coffee, Arabica and Robusta, and about sixty per cent of the world's coffee is Arabica.
Brazil produces about one third of the world's coffee, more than any other country. People around the world drink about two billion cups of coffee every day.

Then things changed, because a large factory opened on the edge of town. As a result, most families moved to new houses nearby.

tx.t: Today I would like to talk about the Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef system in the world. It lies off the coast of Queensland in north-eastern Australia.
It stretches for roughly two thousand three hundred kilometres. More than one thousand five hundred species of fish live there, together with many kinds of turtles and sharks.
It was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in nineteen eighty-one. Warm water causes corals to expel the algae that feed them, which turns them white. This is called bleaching.
Scientists say that rising sea temperatures are the greatest long-term threat to the reef.
